reviews.comment: There's nothing to complain about him honestly. He gives homework problems and doesn't grade them. He is overall really caring and I would take his class again.
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Smith is a really kind and caring prof! If you want to succeed in his class do all of the posted hw before recitation. This class has proofs and theorems that need to be memorized so make sure to have them down well! His exams can be tough but he is a kind grader, study hard for exam 3! He is helpful in office hours and replies to emails fast!
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great at giving partial credit, willing to answer questions, homework is optional (but highly recommended to study for tests), and the grades are based on points using 10 quizzes, 3 midterms, and a final. However, the lectures can be boring, the class is proof-heavy, and the content is hard without prior AP Calculus knowledge.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have no experience in calculus, this class would probably be very challenging. The only grades from the class are weekly quizzes, 3 midterms, and a final, with the quizzes averaging out to one midterm. Lots of proofs, but it's always obvious which ones you need to memorize. Dr. Smith is a nice guy and is eager to take questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His quizzes and tests were all based on the homework. If you could figure out how to do most problems, it is very reasonable to get an A. His lectures are quite a bit boring, but his explanations are always extremely accurate. avg test score is around a 70. Be EXTREMELY accurate or suffer a horrid grade (on tests, quizzes are more leniant).
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did pretty bad on his first two exams and I had to perform on the last test. His class basically consistent of him going over proofs to help and explain why certain things were true, helping you grasp why something worked. It was overall a really nice class and I would recommend for you to attend every lecture, as that helped me with the concepts
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good at explaining the basics, but got worse near the middle and end of the course. Get ready to reteach yourself most of the topics. Ensure you are prepared for every quiz and ESPECIALLY for the exams, there is little room for error. The first two exams are similar to the reviews, but the final varied a lot more from the review. Overall nice guy.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith does a decent job of teaching linear algebra. However, most of his teaching style involves just working out textbook problems on the board, so it can be a little hard to understand what he is talking about at times. An A or a B is very doable, but don't expect any room to make mistakes during the exams as they are weighted very high.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Roger Smith is the best math professor I had at Texas A&M. Clear and concise lectures. One can tell he's been doing this for ages the way he responds to questions accurately and clearly. Assessments are not hard, but I walked away feeling like I understood the material.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The grading structure is pretty harsh, as the final grade is made up of only exams and quizzes. The final exam makes up 33% of the grade.

The homework problems he recommends from the textbook often have no correspondence to the quizzes. Material on the quizzes and exams are generally problems straight from lectures, so watch the lecture videos.

The lectures were very boring and pretty useless. Weekly quizzes were pretty easy. Class grade is HEAVILY dependent on exams and quizzes as there are no homework grades. Midterms were pretty easy but the final was brutal.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Smith explains formulas and computations well but doesn't provide a good understanding of what any of it means. No homework, usually easy weekly quizzes, 2 reasonable midterm exams, and a difficult final that properly pulls material from the entire semester, although much of it was obscure. Friendly and answers all questions during class.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy

reviews.comment: Roger Smith is extremely kind as a person. As a professor, he can be boring and gives poor explanations. I had a B for the entire semester until he gave an extremely difficult final exam that covered topics barely covered or discussed in class. He provides no bonus points and the course is very exam heavy, so there is little room for error.

This course feels like what I think college classes should. Quiz every Friday, 2 Tests, 1 Final. Thats It. No homework, no extra credit. Professor Smith gives decent lectures and is always open to questions, but does not always give the most understandable answers. Most quizzes and exams are very reasonable, and adequately test your knowledge.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very test heavy course, with quizzes every Friday. There is no homework, which sounds nice on paper but having no graded motivation to work outside of lecture can sometimes lead to last minute cramming sessions. Tests are super fair, and he gives very good practice exams prior. Lectures aren't the most fun, but he certainly teaches linear algebra.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maybe 10% of the students would actually show up for lecture and it was insanely boring. He would read directly off the slides and write on the whiteboard word for word. I would have an A in the class if it wasn't for the weekly quizzes but they were sometimes hard and there is no padding with homework or anything. You have to  teach yourself
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy

reviews.comment: Grades are VERY test heavy. I got 10s on every quiz w/ mid Bs on Exam 1&2 & still needed to get a mid B to get an A (no HW grades). His lectures were well structured and he'd spend time explaining something if you speak up & ask. I wouldn't take him again b/c the grades don't give you much room to mess up but I liked his lectures.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As far as how math professors go, Prof. Smith is fine. You could do better, but you could also do a lot worse. Only real downside is that lectures are pretty boring, but he's good with reviewing and answering questions. Do homework/practice exams since quizzes and tests are similar and grade is reliant on those.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very nice man and very lenient with makeups. However, he can be very boring during lectures and I personally find it difficult to follow. If you are very good at following along even while bored, definitely take him, but personally, I had to teach myself the whole class by reviewing his notes and watching YouTube videos.

Professor Smith is not a good teacher. It is noteworthy that he is incredibly kind and considerate. In hindsight, I do not think that I learned much, but memorized a ton. Practice exams are very good for you. The book for the course is completely useless, only used for homework questions. I would not take this professor again.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Smith is awesome. He is great at breaking down difficult concepts, and truly cares for his students. The class is clearly structured, with a quiz each week. His exam reviews are lifesavers and make the tests super straightforward! Wish I could've had Smith for all of my math classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Smith was probably one of the worst professors I've ever had, he had pre-written notes that he would just write down on the board for us to copy and he would skip a lot of steps while working the problems, making his lectures hard to follow. I had to basically re-teach myself all of the content we were supposed to have learned in lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is highly intelligent, VERY kind, and humble. JUST TAKE HIM!

You kinda gotta understand that you're taking a college level math course, so it's really not gonna be easy no matter who you get. Professor Smith is pretty much the best you're gonna get. He's straightforward with all his lectures, grading, and what you needed to do to pass. If you pay attention and do the hw you have a good chance of passing
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Smith was one of those professors that has pre written notes and reads them out loud word for word. He has one quiz a week that are relatively alright if u study the notes. reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I can confirm, Roger Smith is not the greatest linear algebra professor. I did not learn much from his actual lectures, it was hard to follow his hand written notes everyday in class and I had to basically learn everything on my own. Not worth taking linear algebra with him unless you've taken it before in HS or you will be very lost ngl.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is a great professor, his lectures were a little slow, so it might be hard to stay focused during his lectures, but you should be fine for the most part as long as you do his assigned homework and prepare for the weekly quizzes.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you are looking for someone is who straight forward and has good notes, this is your guy. If you had a question, he always answered it without making you even more confused *cough cough 99% of other professors cough* Tests were fair, but more on the hard side. His practice exams are usually much easier than the actual test.

Prof. Smith is probably one of the better linear algebra teachers. His notes were straight to the point. Make sure to do the homework. The quizzes forced me to stay on top on his class so I thought they were really helpful. He's a really sweet guy and helps out a lot during office hours and is very accessible with emails.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is an ez class, NOT! There's optional HW, don't do & you're toast b/c of weekly QZ. reviews.comment: Dr. Smith's lectures are pretty boring. It can be very hard to pay attention for an hour and fifteen minutes. This class required a lot of learning on my own outside of class. reviews.comment: Decent lecturer if a bit slow going at times. He's very theoretical however which was weird for an engineering course. reviews.comment: The bestest professor ever. The class itself is not hard, but not just easy either; you GOTTA take VERY good note and NOT miss a single class. Do the work, you be fine

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a very good prof. I had him for 172 and 171. He does not make hw due, but does give problems to help you. Quizzes once a week help you stay on track. reviews.comment: His lectures may be boring but they hold everything you need to understand the material. There are weekly quizzes and he drops the lowest quiz grade. reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is amazing and is really sweet and helpful. reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a good prof, and he is very nice. If you raise your hand and ask for clarification he is more than willing to help. reviews.comment: Dr. Smith has a really hard time connecting his explanations of Probability to how you actually are supposed to solve his problems.
